sections.h2: Can a Plantation homeowner sell for cash on a short timeline?
sections.html:
Yes. With no mortgage involved, a cash purchase in Plantation moves at the speed of the title search, the payoffs and the deed signing. A traditional listing adds an appraisal, an inspection round and loan approval for the buyer.

Plantation sits in Broward County, directly west of Fort Lauderdale. The city counted 94,288 residents in 2018, and home values in town ranged from $125,000 to over $2 million, with a median of $271,200. The Broward County Property Appraiser has current values, since these numbers are old. Commuters bound for Fort Lauderdale, Miami or the port ask first about access to I-95, I-595 and I-75, so open with your commute when you talk to any buyer.

Think about what you need most: speed, price or certainty. A seller facing an estate, a move or a code problem often values a fixed closing date. A seller with a well-kept house and no deadline can test the market with an agent first and still keep a cash offer as a fallback.

  • Cash fits deferred repairs, code issues or a tenant in place.
  • A listing fits a house that shows well while demand is strong.
  • Estates and liens need paperwork under either path.

sections.h2: Why lot sizes vary across Plantation
sections.html:
Frederick Peters bought 10,000 acres along State Road 7 in the 1930s and hired architect Russell Pancoast to plan a city. The plan barred neighboring homes from looking alike, set minimum lot sizes and divided land into residential, commercial and industrial zones. His idea of long acres offered one-acre lots, with two thirds kept for gardens and fruit trees.

Plantation incorporated on April 30, 1953. Later annexations pushed the western edge out to Flamingo Road, roughly seven miles from State Road 7, so the west is newer than the east. A Plantation Acres lot looks nothing like a house out west. Tell buyers which side you are on, because lot size and building age differ across town and both move the price.

With heavy rain and heat, inspectors look hard at roofs, drainage and air conditioning. Pull together permits and service records before anyone visits.

sections.h2: Recreation and amenities that help a sale
sections.html:
Parks and golf help sell houses in Plantation. The city operates the Plantation Preserve Golf Course and Club, and newer parks include Plantation Woods in the historic district and Camp Everglades at Volunteer Park. The Helen B. Hoffman Plantation Library serves residents alongside the county's West Regional Library, and the city lists Nova Southeastern University, Florida Atlantic University, Broward College and McFatter Technical Center within a 10 minute drive.

Plantation Gateway, Plantation Midtown and Plantation Technology Park offer jobs close to home. The airport is 15 minutes away by the city's count, with Tri-Rail, Amtrak and county buses also in reach.

  • List the park or golf course closest to your address.
  • Name your school zone only after confirming it with the district.
  • Stay factual in your descriptions.

sections.h2: Closing charges on a Plantation deed
sections.html:
The deed stamp tax in Broward is the statewide 70 cents on every $100. Recording costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per added page. Because each party named on the deed can be held liable for the tax, the contract should say who pays it.

Have the title agent list every charge, payoffs included, before you commit to a closing date.

Expect the stamp tax, recording charges, payoffs, prorated taxes and any association fees to appear on one settlement statement. Compare it with your contract several days ahead so a surprise does not delay the signing. If a charge looks wrong, the title agent can explain it or fix it before closing.

Broward assessment limits
RuleLimit
Homestead exemptionUp to $50,000, apply by March 1
Homestead yearly growthLower of 3 percent or inflation (2.9 percent for 2025, 2.7 percent for 2026)
Other property yearly growth10 percent
Portability to a new homesteadWithin three years

To qualify, the house must have been your residence on January 1. After a sale, the buyer is reassessed at market value the next January 1, so your capped value stays with you, not the house. Portability lets you move savings to another Florida homestead. If you dispute a bill, the value adjustment board process applies, with deadlines printed on your August notice. Broward's offices can quote the current millage for your address.

sections.h2: What if my house has a foreclosure, an estate or a tenant?
sections.html:
Any of the three can still end in a sale. The clerk sells a foreclosed house 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the date is pushed back, and the winning bidder puts down a 5 percent deposit. Estates worth $150,000 or less may use summary administration, and Florida's estate tax stopped applying to deaths after 2004. In a rental, unpaid rent starts with a three-day notice, and a monthly tenancy ends with 30 days' notice.

If the house is rented, tell the tenant in writing that a sale is under way, and keep showings to reasonable hours. The lease stays in force after the sale unless it ends on its own terms, so the buyer takes the house with the tenant in it. For an estate, the person with court authority signs, and the title agent will ask for that paperwork before setting a closing date. For a foreclosure, speed matters most: a buyer who can close before the auction date can pay the lender and leave you with whatever equity remains.

Talk to a Florida attorney before anyone signs a deed for an estate or for an owner in default.

1. Gather payoff letters, tax bill and tenant information.
  2. Review written offers for the price, closing day and repair terms.
  3. The title agent clears the record.
  4. You sign the deed in front of two witnesses.
  5. Broward's clerk records it and funds are released.

Keep your recorded deed with your tax records. Ask each buyer when funds will be available, who orders the title policy and whether an inspection can change the offer. Houses in Plantation run from modest single-family homes to properties worth well over $1 million, so the pool of buyers and the paperwork shift with price. Owners of higher-value houses should raise payoffs, survey needs and association approvals with the title agent at the start.

Start with a short packet: your payoff letter, the latest tax bill, any survey you have, and a list of repairs or permits you know about. The title agent can open the file and order the record search the same day, which is what keeps a cash timeline short. Keep a copy of every page you sign.

Choosing cash means no repairs, no staging and no waiting on a buyer's bank. Lien payoffs, the tax proration and the signing remain, and they take a few days. With tenants in the house, pass the lease and deposit records to the buyer before closing.

faqs.q: Which county records a Plantation deed?
Why do Plantation lot sizes vary so much?
faqs.a: A 1930s master plan set minimum lot sizes, and later annexation added western land out to Flamingo Road, so older and newer areas differ.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Broward?
faqs.a: Recording is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, and the 70 cents per $100 stamp tax applies on top.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The buyer is assessed at market value starting the next January 1.

faqs.q: Where can I find current home values?
faqs.a: The Broward County Property Appraiser. City figures from 2018 are background only.
